items.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: she wanted me to do a couple, I don't know that I did a whole lot of arrangements for her. I did a couple of arrangements for her.

ctx.x: All right, get my paper situated here. We're talking more the vocal arranging you did. First of all, before we even get to that, how'd you go into, I understand you had a studio. Talk about that.

Yes. What happened was that when I came out of the Navy, I decided that I would open a studio. I had ?? and she had a studio bass player by the name of Doles Dickens and do writing, you know write for special material and for singers and stuff like that and coaching. And it was during that time right after … I guess, when did I come out of the Navy, '46 or something like that … and I hadn't set up more than, not very long, for months of something. Anyway, Lena Horne evidently needed an arranger and music…
You said working with Lena was a learning experience. Exactly what did you learn?
